prompt:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.

assessments.name: Identity
assessments.instructions:
Identity should answer: Is this a real business, and is it the one it claims to be?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity

assessments.name: Activity
assessments.instructions:
What does this business actually do, and is it allowed to do it?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.

assessments.name: Ownership
assessments.instructions:
Who actually controls and benefits from this business?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers

assessments.name: Compliance
assessments.instructions:
Is this business, or anyone behind it, someone we're prohibited or restricted from doing business with?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits

result.headline: Onboard subject to conditions: a beneficial ownership certification, a statement of activity and permits, and PEP and adverse media screening.

body.text: The name, the address and the one person submitted all resolve to a single California filing made in February 2022. There is no foreign registration and no second record to reconcile, and the state publishes a sub-status, so standing is settled rather than inferred from the filing being active.

The only address on the record is an apartment that no other business files from, which is the ordinary footprint for a small owner-operated LLC formed from home. It places the filer, not the trade: nothing on the record carries a second location, a website or a third-party profile.

MICHAEL N ELLENBURG is on the filing in the registered-agent capacity and matches there. No member or manager appears anywhere on the record, so the entity is established and the people behind it are not; that is taken up under Ownership.

gaps.point: No website or third-party profile is on the record, so nothing outside the state filing corroborates that the business is trading

body.text: Nothing on the record classifies the activity. The registered name is the only account of the line of work, and coffee is neither a restricted nor a prohibited line; but with no industry classification, website or profile behind it, there is equally nothing that would surface a second activity if one existed.

No licence data was returned for this record, so whether the county health and state seller's permits a food and beverage operation needs are held, and in whose name, is not established. The residential filing address gives no trading premises to check them against.

gaps.point: What the business actually sells and where it trades from, beyond what its registered name implies
Whether the permits a San Diego food and beverage operation requires are held, and whether they are held by the entity or by an individual

body.text: The single person the customer submitted is the agent of record. An agent appointment is a service-of-process obligation and says nothing about who holds or controls the LLC, so the only verified individual on this file is verified in a capacity that does not answer the question.

Nothing else stands behind the entity: no member or manager is published, and no corporate owner, parent or affiliate sits above it. The structure is therefore single-layer and simple to certify, but ownership and control rest entirely on what the customer attests to.

gaps.point: Who holds 25 percent or more of the LLC and who exercises control, and whether MICHAEL N ELLENBURG is among them or is only the agent of record

body.text: CHARM COFFEE LLC and MICHAEL N ELLENBURG were screened against sanctions and watchlists, and the entity was checked for litigation, liens and bankruptcy. PEP and adverse media screening has not been run against either name, and no other person is named on the record to screen.

gaps.point: Whether CHARM COFFEE LLC or MICHAEL N ELLENBURG appears on a PEP list or in adverse media
Whether anyone who holds or controls the business, beyond the agent of record, is on a sanctions, PEP or adverse media list

followUps.text: Collect the beneficial ownership certification and screen each individual it names. The filing carries MICHAEL N ELLENBURG as registered agent only, no member or manager is published, and the screening on file therefore reaches the entity and its agent and nobody who owns or controls it.

Obtain a written statement of the business's activity, its trading location, and any county health or seller's permit held. No industry classification, website or profile is on the record, and the only address on file is the residential one the LLC was formed at.

Order PEP and adverse media screening for CHARM COFFEE LLC and MICHAEL N ELLENBURG. Only the watchlist screen was run, so nothing on the record speaks to political exposure or to negative news against either name.
